title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: Exploration of CLO Virtual Clothing Teaching and Research
description: CLO Academic Month 2024 Review! Teacher Ren Jinhui from the School of Fashion Art and Engineering at Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology prepared teaching materials based on her own software learning experience, anticipating students' questions in advance to help them learn more effectively. She utilized the virtual model editing function in CLO to simulate various body types for special groups to assist in design projects. Click the video to see Teacher Ren share CLO's functional clothing design case studies.

summary: # CLO 2024 Academic Month: Exploration of CLO Virtual Clothing Teaching and Research ## Introduction Today, I'm going to talk about the subject of my talk, which is the study of virtual fashion and the exploration of science and technology. As soon as you hear this, you'll know that there are two parts to it: one is teaching, and the other is science and technology. Today, I'm going to share three parts. 1. The first part is to introduce the courses related to virtual fashion, especially the one I'm teaching. 2. The second part is about the problems I encountered during my teaching process and how I solved them. 3. The third part is about how we apply virtual fashion to science and technology. ## Background President Jia has already introduced me, so I won't go into details. I graduated from Beijing Fashion College and then went to an outdoor clothing company. After that, I returned to school, where I gave the school's creative products a brand name of Bift Collection. I started to work on projects such as the Winter Olympics, the National Day, the 70th Anniversary Exhibition, and so on. My current focus is on functional clothing design, which mainly focuses on sports, disabled people, elderly individuals, and classmates. ## Courses on Virtual Clothing Currently, we are working on a series of courses related to virtual clothing, which includes a number of courses. Among them are digital clothing technology courses. ### Digital Clothing Technology Courses The first course was taught by Professor Ma Kai at our school and started in 2019. Our school has been the first to establish a digital experiment class since 2019. In this experiment class, there were 30 students in the first year: 20 students were in design, and 10 students were in the field of clothing factories. The classes they took were pretty much the same. In the first year of high school, the 30 students in the lab took exams related to their major, English, and various intelligence monitoring questions. Last year, in 2023, we graduated from the first digital experiment class established in 2019. I participated in their graduation design and thesis. ### Digital Costume Textile Technology Course Let me introduce the most intimate course we took, called Digital Costume Textile Technology. The picture on the bottom left is a scene from my class, where we are in the digital experiment class, the art class, the fashion design course, and the graduate course. There are 36 courses in total. During these courses, we teach both theory and practice, which is the main focus. The basic principles and concepts provide knowledge of the current digital and virtual costumes and concepts closely related to them. The next stage includes the behavioral and physical changes of virtual models, the simulation and production of common costumes, the texture of the fabric and production methods, the setting and rendering of scenes, and finally, we use a comprehensive class assignment to submit the homework. ### Examples of Course Content What you see on this page are some examples we used in the teaching process. For example, in the first class, we introduce a very simple shirt or pants and assign homework to the students first. This helps us gauge their level of understanding. In previous classes, we used relatively short sessions to introduce the applications of virtual clothing software, so most students have already been in contact with it. Some students who are more interested may have already learned part of it through teaching videos available online. We use this application to teach the students, aiming to assess their comprehension levels, which, in general, are not very good. Most students struggle with the software initially, although there are a few who have self-learned and performed well. ### Virtual Model Adjustments The bottom right corner of this page shows a virtual model and how to adjust the model's posture in the 3D window. The white mold in the middle represents an elderly person's body shape. We used an OBJ file to teach students how to manipulate the model's body shape and makeup. As for the clothing, the one in the back is a revision case before the final version. We utilized some of Beifu's original design cases to illustrate this process. We extracted patterns from photos using tools like Photoshop or PixPlant to create various textile designs. ## Course Themes In the first eight classes, we covered models, fabrics, clothing, and related topics. After the teaching sessions, we introduce a theme for the class, which varies each semester. For example, the themes for the last semester, which just ended in 2023, included: 1. Cyberpunk 2. Artificial Intelligence 3. Sustainable Design 4. Traditional Clothing Restoration and Innovation These themes have been trending in recent years. The festival was held at the end of the year to coincide with Christmas, New Year, and the Spring Festival. We also incorporated themes related to rural revitalization, matching projects that Beifu and Di Shang Group undertook to develop clothing for farmers and shepherds. ## Student Projects and Competitions Students often draw inspiration from design competitions. More experienced students might take the lead in such competitions. In the last class, we focused on fashion engineering. Science students, who did not have a background in design, tended to choose traditional clothing themes, while design students leaned towards innovative design for clothing structures. The students' work showcased their understanding of traditional themes and incorporated their creativity. For instance, some students designed minority ethnic clothing with modified patterns, while others explored cyber themes, focusing on the combination of machines and people. ### Graduation Design Examples In addition to the digital clothing course, I would like to show you some graduation projects from 2020, which was our first digital experiment class. One student focused on water as a design element, creating folds inspired by water patterns. His thesis explored methods for creating folds in 3D software. Another student utilized ceramic patterns and presented a design that made it to the cover of our last year's fashion week. His thesis analyzed the 3D printing process involved in his work. ## Teaching Challenges Now, I would like to discuss some problems I encountered during the teaching process. ### Issues in Student Learning The first challenge is that students from different professional backgrounds have varying speeds and creativity levels. The software we use has many tools, which can be overwhelming for beginners. To address this, we implemented several supporting tools, such as recording demonstration processes for students to review later. Based on my own experience, I summarized methods to help students familiarize themselves with the software and provided them with instruction manuals containing screenshots and key processes. This way, students could catch up or advance their learning at their own pace. ### Common Questions and Issues Additionally, I observed that students often asked basic questions about finding tools or importing files. They also struggled with craftsmanship and understanding the sewing process, especially since many were not familiar with fabric and garment construction. Another recurring problem was 3D space conversion, where students struggled to differentiate between front and back or left and right when manipulating patterns. ### Software Challenges Students also frequently encountered issues with threading, cracking, and folding while using the software. Despite emphasizing solutions in class, some students continued to face these challenges. ## Application of Virtual Clothing in Research In the earlier stages of my work with Beifu, I focused on functional clothing for disabled individuals. The Kangjian Clothing Research Center was established in 2008, later evolving into the Wuzhai Clothing Research Center in 2018, and now it's called the Beautiful Life Clothing Research Center. Before the Beijing East Olympic Games, I collaborated with the Ministry of Science and Technology to develop clothing for the National Team of the Winter Olympic Games, applying virtual software for their specialized sports apparel. We also conducted research into clothing for the elderly, collecting body data and using it to create designs tailored to their needs. This research is ongoing, with some projects still in progress. ### Digital Experiment Class Graduation Design The digital experiment class graduation designs reflect the culmination of students' learning and creativity. Some designs have been created for wheelchair users, demonstrating how virtual clothing can contribute to functional and innovative solutions in fashion. That's all for my sharing today. Thank you for listening!
